paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: no chain, no tomb and no crowd of demons is too much for Jesus. Nobody had the strength to subdue this man (Mark 5:4), and a whole legion was living in him. Jesus spoke, and they had to ask HIS permission to go anywhere (Mark 5:12-13). Whatever has a grip on you, it doesn't outrank Him.

Now look at the two responses. The people in the region saw the man sitting there, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid, and they began to beg Jesus to leave (Mark 5:15, 17). The man who had been freed begged to go WITH Him (Mark 5:18). I think that tells us something: when Jesus shows up and changes things, some people want Him gone, and some want to stay close forever. Friend, I know which side of that drawer I'd rather be on.

But Jesus gave the man a job instead. He said, “Go home to your own people,” and then, “tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.” (Mark 5:19) The man didn't need a big speech, only his own story, and he told it all over the Decapolis, and everyone was amazed (Mark 5:20). So when Jesus has done something for you, tell somebody, because that's how a comeback gets passed on.
